en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Twenty-first Chapter
Regarding the discourse on the Dhamma: Are all phenomena fixed? Yes.
Are they fixed in wrongness?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Are they fixed in rightness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “There is no group of the undetermined”?
It should not be said thus … [as before] …
Is it not the case that there is an indeterminate group?
Yes, it is.
If indeed there is an indeterminate group, then surely you should not say this:
“All phenomena are fixed.
Are all phenomena fixed? Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One that there are three groups:
"the group fixed in falsehood, the group fixed in truth, and the undetermined group"?
Yes, it was.
If three groups were indeed spoken of by the Blessed One—
“the group fixed in falsehood, the group fixed in truth, and the group not fixed”— then surely it should not be said that “all phenomena are fixed.”
Is form determined in the sense of being form?
Yes. Is it determined in the sense of being fixed in wrongness? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that it is fixed in rightness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] …
Feeling … perception … mental formations … [and so forth] … consciousness.
Is consciousness determined in the sense of being consciousness?
Yes. Is it determined for falsehood? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that it is fixed in rightness?
It should not be said thus … [as before].
It should not be said that form is fixed in the sense of being form … [and so on] … feeling … [and so on] …
Are perception … formations … consciousness determined in the sense of being consciousness?
“Yes.
“Is form feeling? … pe … Is it perception?”
There are volitional formations;
there is consciousness; there is feeling ... [and so on] ... pe ... [as before] ... pe ... [end].
Perception ... [and so on] ...
volitional formations ...
[and so on] ... consciousness is form ... [and so on].
Is there feeling?
Is there perception?
Are there volitional formations?
It should not be stated thus.
For in that case, matter is determined in the sense of being matter; feeling … perception … [and so on].
Volitional formations...
consciousness is established in the sense of consciousness.
The Discourse on Dhamma is finished.
